note: FNS 843 is a QC review procedure describing how reviewers should handle error determinations when household composition variances are found: 'most variances will be handled by simply adding or subtracting the individual(s) and their circumstances from the household.' This is audit methodology guidance for QC reviewers, not a caseworker policy requirement. It tells reviewers how to recalculate benefits after finding a composition error — a function that has no caseworker equivalent. The underlying caseworker-facing policy (how to add/remove household members and account for their income, assets, and circumstances) is well covered in the OLG under 'SNAP > Eligibility Requirements > Household Composition' including pages on adding new members (with BEACON procedures), nonhousehold members, and treatment of disqualified/ineligible members' income. The OLG also covers overissuance calculation when composition errors are discovered after the fact under 'Cross Programs > Overpayments and Recovery'. But FNS 843 itself is about QC error determination methodology, not a policy standard the OLG needs to implement.
